transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, your clinical conversational agent. I conducted your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have some questions. First, I'm wondering when I can start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can start light gardening, such as brisk walking, gardening, light jogging, and gentle cycling, about 1 week after surgery. However, it's best to avoid strenuous or heavy exercise, lifting heavy objects, pilates or yoga, or swimming for a month. Also, be sure to wear protective eyewear when doing any physical activity. Does that help? Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That helps a lot, thank you. My second question is when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can start using preservative-free eye drops for dry eyes four times a day, as soon as you need them. If you were already using eye drops before your surgery, you can continue using them unless you were told otherwise. If you're running out, your GP should be able to provide some more. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Got it, thank you for clarifying. I have another question: I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Yes, it's normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to the new lenses. However, if it's severe or accompanied by redness and pain, we may need to assess it further. If it's just mild, wearing sunglasses when you're outside might help. Does that help? Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, that helps. My last question is about blurriness—should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time. If your vision is still blurry, or getting significantly worse or blurry, we may need to check it to make sure it's okay. It's also possible that you may need reading glasses or varifocals for reading, especially if it's the only part of your vision that's blurry. Does that make sense?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, that makes sense. Thank you for all the information. I don't have any more questions right now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It was my pleasure to help. I'm glad I could answer your questions. Now, I just need to confirm: do you feel like all your questions about your cataract surgery recovery have been answered?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all my questions have been answered. Thank you for your help!
